_comment_yield_average_horizon_turns: The forward-projection horizon (in turns) for a source's steady realized yield. SourceYield.realized is the AVERAGE food/turn the source delivers over the next N turns, computed by simulating the herd/patch forward N turns from its current state under the assignment's policy + worker count (the smooth policy rate, no kill-credit bank). A pure function of state, so the assign-time seed and the resolved row are identical (exact forecast==actual). Larger = a herd settled at its floor reads flat ≈ the regrowth there, and a projection under a LOWER floor sees the herd's decline within the window. Its OWN lever, NOT the expedition forecast_horizon_turns (a raid-length horizon). PLAYTEST DIAL. Validated > 0.
_comment_arrivals_horizon_turns: The forward-projection horizon (in turns) for a source's ARRIVAL SCHEDULE. SourceYield.arrivals[i] is the food landing i+1 turns from now, from the SAME forward simulation the realized average runs but WITH the kill-credit bank — so it answers 'on which turns does the food actually arrive', not 'how much per turn on average'. A big-game hunt at a high floor is genuinely lumpy (zeros between hauls); a forage patch or fast game lands something every turn. Kept SEPARATE from yield_average_horizon_turns (40) deliberately: this is a display span (how far ahead the larder chart plans), that one is a smoothing window. PLAYTEST DIAL. Validated > 0.

forage._comment_capacity_by_biome: THE HUMAN FOOD WEB, BY BIOME — the exact mirror of fauna_config.json's graze.capacity_by_biome (the ANIMAL food web), and the other half of the two-stock split (docs/plan_grazing_foundation.md §1). Human-edible biomass (seeds, nuts, tubers, fruit, shellfish, inshore fish) a tile of each biome carries at capacity; every FoodModuleTag tile is seeded a patch at its biome's value, and a biome reading 0 carries NO PATCH AT ALL. A DATA TABLE OVER THE 38 BIOMES, NOT A FORMULA: every biome must appear (validate() rejects a partial table — a missing row would silently read as an invisible zero-forage dead zone; ZERO MUST BE STATED). Per-BIOME, not per-FoodModule, deliberately: the two tables must be directly comparable tile-for-tile and must be able to DISAGREE WITHIN a module — that disagreement is the agropastoral decision. The FoodModuleTag model is untouched; the module still says what KIND of gathering a tile offers (and its seasonal_weight), this table says HOW MUCH is there. THE HEADLINE INVERSIONS, against the graze table: MixedWoodland 190 forage vs 55 graze (nuts, mast, berries under a canopy that shades out the ground cover — the flagship case); Floodplain/RiverDelta/AlluvialPlain 195-210 forage vs 130-140 graze (silt + water = CROPLAND, the farm, not the pasture); PrairieSteppe 70 forage vs 240 graze (grass: the animals feast, the humans get seed heads). Retired: the old flat carrying_capacity of 120 on every food-module tile, which made one food web spatial and the other a constant and so made 'your best farm is not your best pasture' UNTRUE BY CONSTRUCTION.
forage._comment_cultivation_moved_dials: The plant rung-2 BUILD dials (progress_per_turn, decay_per_turn and the old cultivating_yield_fraction) live in intensification_ladder.json -> the plant:tended rung's `build` block, and as of slice 4 so do the earned-knowledge dials (the old knowledge_progress_per_turn 0.05 / knowledge_completion_threshold 1.0 -> the ladder's `knowledge` block, same values, previously duplicated verbatim in fauna_config's husbandry). Both food webs climb — and now LEARN — on the same numbers. What remains here is the plant web's own economy.
forage._comment_cultivation: THE PLANT LADDER'S PAYOFFS — what each completed rung buys you. The BUILD dials (how long each rung takes, its feral decay, its investment dip) live in intensification_ladder.json; only the payoffs are here, exactly as fauna_config keeps pastoral_gain/pen_gain beside the ladder's build block. A TILE'S PRODUCTION IS CONSTANT ACROSS RUNGS 1-3 (issue #433, docs/plan_flora_roster.md §4.3): the LAND owns K, no rung below 4 raises it and NONE LOWERS IT, so what a rung changes is only WHICH PLANTS that constant production is made of — and every yield rate (food, fodder, trade) is the share-weighted average of the patch's effective basket, at every rung including wild. THE TWO RUNGS PAY IN DIFFERENT CURRENCIES, AND THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE MODEL (slice 7): RUNG 2 (tended) IS STILL A WILD STAND, better cared for — but since Flora Roster S2 a NEUTRAL one: its patch regrows at the WILD rate (tended_regrowth_gain 1.0), and you gather it under the full escapement-floor dial, drawing it down and able to over-farm it, exactly as a wild patch. What tending buys is WEEDING (tended_weeding_gain, see _comment_weeding) plus CONVERSION: tended_conversion_gain multiplies the FAVORED species' WHOLE YIELD VECTOR — food, fodder and trade alike, no role branch — and NOTHING ELSE in the basket, because tending is knowing YOUR crop and the volunteers standing beside it are still wild. A blanket multiplier on the whole basket would make every commitment pay ~gain regardless of what you favored, which erases the crop choice; on the favored term it COMPOUNDS with weeding, so favoring a dominant plant pays and favoring a marginal one barely moves. RUNG 3 (field) IS YOURS — you control its reproduction, so the basket is 100% the crop, there is no wild stock left to over-skim, the policy axis honestly collapses, and it pays a flat managed rate on its standing crop without drawdown (the pen's twin), scaled by the DERIVED patch_species_quality (the projected basket's rate over the wild baseline) rather than a second per-species dial. Rung 3 does NOT take the tended conversion gain — field_provisions_per_biomass is its own dial. RETIRED: tended_provisions_per_biomass 0.01, which made rung 2 a managed rate a full rung EARLIER than the animal side. S2 RETIRED THE REGROWTH BOOST (tended_regrowth_gain 2.0 -> 1.0, NEUTRAL) on the grounds that competitor-removal was already explicit, and left rung 2's payoff owing; tended_conversion_gain (2.0) is what pays that debt — the term that makes a 25-turn Cultivate recoup in the teens of turns rather than the eighties. The regrowth lever stays (1.0 = neutral, a playtest dial if a small boost is wanted back). VALIDATED: field_provisions_per_biomass > tended_regrowth_gain x regrowth_rate/4 x provisions_per_biomass x tended_conversion_gain (tended < field, still monotone and scale-free) — evaluated at tending's SATURATED best case, where the basket is the favored crop alone and that crop's own rate cancels from both sides, which is what keeps the check independent of which species it is asked about; tended_regrowth_gain only forbids the INCOHERENT case gain < 1.0 (tending making a stand grow SLOWER than wild). PLAYTEST DIALS.
forage._comment_weeding: THE LAND OWNS K, AND NO RUNG BELOW 4 RAISES IT **OR LOWERS IT** (issue #433, docs/plan_flora_roster.md §4.3). Committing a patch to one named plant (Cultivate/Sow, flora_config.json) does not change how much the tile produces — it changes WHAT THAT PRODUCTION IS MADE OF. TENDED (rung 2) WEEDS: the favored species' share rises to min(1.0, share x tended_weeding_gain) and the increase is taken from the LEAST ABUNDANT REMAINING SPECIES FIRST (ties by species key ascending), so the smallest weeds go first and the basket still sums to 1. FIELD (rung 3) PLANTS: the favored share is forced to 1.0 and every other to 0 — you sowed it, there are no volunteers. LEAST ABUNDANT FIRST IS DELIBERATE AND IS NOT 'LOWEST-YIELDING': ranking the weeds by yield would mean comparing a food rate against a trade rate, an exchange rate this codebase does not have and should not invent, and hay_grass (0 food, 0 trade, 0.2 fodder) has no non-arbitrary rank at all. Abundance is currency-free, deterministic from the composition alone, and independent of which crop was favored. WHAT THIS REPLACED: a CONCENTRATION term that multiplied the tile's K by min(1, share x gain) and DISCARDED the remainder, so committing a patch to a marginal plant CUT its production — the bug #433 fixed. effective_forage_capacity / patch_concentration / concentration_for_share and the field_concentration_gain dial (2.5) are retired with it; a Field forces the share to 1.0, so there is no gain left to tune. The cap at 1.0 is the model, not a safety rail: a basket is a whole, weeding can only move share WITHIN it, which is why rung 2's payoff has to come from tended_conversion_gain compounding with a bigger share rather than from the share alone. Validated finite and >= 1.0: below 1 a rung would weed AGAINST the crop it just committed to. PLAYTEST DIAL.
forage._comment_navigable_river: The capacity_by_biome NavigableRiver row (130) is VESTIGIAL — a navigable hex now reads its UNDERLYING biome (resource_terrain) plus navigable_river_forage_bonus, so the row is bypassed. Left only to keep the table total.
